summary: General-purpose web-based assessment items — quizzes, tests and practice questions that render and score in a browser with no assessment platform behind them.
in_scope: Multiple choice — a stem and options, one correct answer
Multi-select ("select all that apply") via max-choices, with several correct options
Per-option points, weighted answers, and partial credit
Exact-set scoring via response-processing "match-correct" — every correct option and nothing else, or zero
Penalized distractors (an option that costs a point when selected)
A rationale on an option, shown once the candidate selects it and withheld from the presentation
Shuffled option order, and author-named option ids
Saying how many selections a question wants via min-choices and max-choices — the candidate is told "Select exactly 2" or "Select up to 3, at least 1"
Unscored polls — an item that collects a response without grading it
Multi-part items over a reading passage with numbered paragraphs, scored additively or conjunctively (both parts right for the point)
Hot text - clicking a sentence inside the passage, as a part of an item or standing alone
Click-the-word vocabulary items via granularity "word", where the candidate words are authored
Select any N of several correct answers via upper-bound, rather than requiring all of them
Written responses via extended-text - collected, held with their rubric and an optional exemplar, and marked by a person; never auto-scored

Fill in the blank via text-entry - one or more blanks in a sentence, each recognizing a list of answers with per-answer score, partial credit, penalties and rationale, and optional case sensitivity per blank
Numeric blanks via base-type "float" or "integer" - the typed answer is compared as a number, so 0.50, .5, 1/2 and 5e-1 all equal 0.5, with an optional tolerance for rounded answers
Requiring a written form with input-formats - decimal, fraction or scientific, for a question that asks the student to express an answer a particular way; the default numeric accepts all of them
Refusing a repeating answer such as 1/3 that no decimal can reach, unless the blank asks for a fraction or carries a tolerance
out_of_scope: Interaction types other than choice, hottext, text-entry and extended-text - ordering, matching, classification, hotspot, sliders and inline dropdowns are not implemented yet
Test packages, sections, navigation and sequencing — L0180 authors single items
Delivery policy — timing, attempt limits, feedback timing, gradebooks
Vendor-specific formats — name the vendor and use that vendor's dialect instead
Images, audio and video — a stimulus is a title and paragraphs of text and every prompt is a plain string, so nothing here places a diagram, a chart or a clip
Standards alignment, depth of knowledge, grade level and the rest of item metadata — an item carries no such fields and nothing in delivery reads them
Export to QTI, Learnosity or any interchange format — compiled output is JSON for the browser. It uses QTI's own field names, so a serializer is possible later, but none exists
Auto-scoring a written response - extended-text emits a rubric and holds the answer for a person; nothing here judges prose

Expressions, units and symbolic equivalence - a numeric blank understands whole numbers, decimals, simple fractions and scientific notation; 1/2 + 1/3, 5 cm and x/2 are not evaluated, nothing judges algebraic equivalence, and a fraction is not checked for lowest terms
